I ran 8 cold launches of BenchTarget on device `<REDACTED-1>` (real Pixel, Android), navigating Home → About → Diagnostics each time with `stopApp: true` to force a fresh process. Results:

| Trial | Build channel | Sync status | "Retry sync" button |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | BENCH-STABLE | Sync idle | ✅ visible |
| 2 | BENCH-STABLE | Sync idle | ✅ visible |
| 3 | BENCH-STABLE | Sync unavailable | ❌ absent |
| 4 | BENCH-STABLE | Sync idle | ✅ visible |
| 5 | BENCH-STABLE | Sync unavailable | ❌ absent |
| 6 | BENCH-STABLE | Sync idle | ✅ visible |
| 7 | BENCH-STABLE | Sync idle | ✅ visible |
| 8 | BENCH-STABLE | Sync unavailable | ❌ absent |

5/8 idle (button shown), 3/8 unavailable (button gone) — matching the reported ~3-in-5 pass rate almost exactly.

**Root cause:** the "Retry sync" button is not hidden/disabled when sync is unavailable — it's *entirely absent from the Compose view hierarchy* (confirmed via `inspect_screen`: the "Sync status" card only contains two TextViews, no Button node, when status reads "Sync unavailable"). Its rendering is conditional on the app's simulated `Sync status`, which is **not** deterministic.

I also confirmed the randomization happens **once per process, at cold start**, not per screen visit: after landing on Diagnostics in the "idle" state, I backed out to Home and re-navigated to Diagnostics *without* relaunching the app — the state stayed "Sync idle" (button still present). Only a fresh cold launch (new process) produced a different roll. The Build channel string (BENCH-STABLE) was constant across all runs, so it's specifically the sync-status simulation that's the variable, and the About screen explicitly states the app "has no network access," so this isn't a real connectivity check — it's an in-app simulated/random value seeded fresh on each process start.

**Flake source:** BenchTarget picks its Diagnostics "sync status" via an unseeded/time-seeded random draw once per app process (roughly ~60% "Sync idle," ~40% "Sync unavailable" from this sample). The "Retry sync" button only renders in the "idle" branch. Since the UI test cold-launches the app for each run, it gets a new random draw each time, so the button assertion passes only on the "idle" runs — reproducing the observed ~3/5 pass rate.

**Fix direction:** the test shouldn't assert unconditional visibility of "Retry sync" against a non-deterministic app state. Either the app needs a deterministic/injectable sync state for test builds (e.g., a debug flag or test hook that forces "idle"), or the test should branch on the "Sync status" text and only assert the button when status is "idle."
